citations.quote: The primary efficacy endpoint was the percent change from baseline in glucocorticoid (GC) daily dose (in hydrocortisone equivalents adjusted for body surface area [BSA] in mg/m2/day) at
Week 24 while also achieving Week 24 androstenedione levels in the controlled range (i.e., \le 120\% of baseline or \le \text{ULN} for age and sex).
Number treated: 181

Planned: 165
Actual: 182

result.text: Glucocorticoid daily dose lowered by 27% (SE 2.4) vs 10% (SE 3.2) placebo at Week 24; treatment difference -17% (95% CI -24, -10). Key secondary: serum androstenedione at Week 4 decreased 299 (37.7) ng/dL vs +46 (51.0) ng/dL placebo; treatment difference -366 ng/dL (95% CI -457, -232). 63% of crinecerfont vs 18% placebo reduced to physiologic glucocorticoid dose at Week 24.

citations.quote: Crinecerfont allowed for lowering of the glucocorticoid daily dose by 27% (2.4) compared to 10% (3.2) in the placebo group at Week 24 while androstenedione levels were controlled. The treatment difference was -17% (95% confidence interval [CI]: -24, -10).

Serum androstenedione at Week 4 was a key secondary endpoint and significantly decreased by 299 (37.7) ng/dL compared to an increase of 46 (51.0) ng/dL in the placebo group. The treatment difference was -366 ng/dL (95% CI: -457, -232).
63% of subjects receiving crinecerfont compared to 18% in the placebo group were able to reduce their daily glucocorticoid dose to the physiologic range

indication.text: Adjunctive treatment to glucocorticoid replacement to control androgens in adults and pediatric patients 4 years of age and older with classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH).

citations.quote: CRENESSITY is indicated as adjunctive treatment to glucocorticoid replacement to control androgens in adults and pediatric patients 4 years of age and older with classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH).

target_moa.text: Crinecerfont is a selective corticotropin-releasing factor (CRF) type 1 receptor antagonist; it blocks CRF binding to pituitary CRF type 1 receptors, inhibiting ACTH secretion and thereby reducing ACTH-mediated adrenal androgen production.

citations.quote: Crinecerfont is a selective corticotropin-releasing factor (CRF) type 1 receptor antagonist. Crinecerfont blocks the binding of CRF to CRF type 1 receptors in the pituitary but not CRF type 2 receptors.
Crinecerfont binding to CRF type 1 receptors inhibits adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) secretion from the pituitary, thereby reducing ACTH-mediated adrenal androgen production.

CRENESSITY contains crinecerfont, a selective corticotropin-releasing factor type 1 receptor antagonist, present as crinecerfont free base, with the chemical name, 2-thiazolamine, 4-(2-chloro-4-methoxy-5-methylphenyl)-N-[(1S)-2-cyclopropyl-1-(3-fluoro-4-methylphenyl)ethyl]-5-methyl-N-2-propyn-1-yl.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions in adults (≥4% and > placebo): fatigue (25% vs 15%), headache (16% vs 15%), dizziness (8% vs 3%), arthralgia (7% vs 0%), back pain (6% vs 3%), decreased appetite (4% vs 2%), myalgia (4% vs 3%). In pediatrics: headache (25% vs 6%), abdominal pain (13% vs 0%), fatigue (7% vs 0%), nasal congestion (7% vs 3%), epistaxis (4% vs 0%). Serious adverse events of acute adrenal insufficiency occurred in both trials in the setting of physiologic stress.
